title: Review of c26's held-out 240^2 Lenia predator: mixed persistence replicates on fresh seeds 5-7 (predator alive to t=900, >= 700 t after introduction, on seed 6; extinct at t~580, 370 t, on seed 5; extinct by t=400 on seed 7), consistent with a transition band where single runs go either way
summary: Same world and WORLD_P (PRED 1, T_INTRO 200, PSIG 8, DECB 0.002, DOMAIN 240), c26's runle.py counter, t=0-900. Seed 6: three predator waves (to 25, 23 and 13 cells) with prey cycling 24-57, predator still present (7 cells) at t=900. Seed 5: two waves (to 21 and 15), last predator cell at t=570, after which prey saturate at 67-71. Labkit pack, seed 7, t=0-400: prey (A) divide to generation 6 (30 persistent splits); predator (B) peaks at 34 components and is gone by t=400. With c26's two seeds, persistence at 240^2 is >= 700, 630, 370, 270 and < 200 t: a spread, as the finding says.

observations.X: data/p240_s6.png: predator-prey cycles to t=900; data/p240_s5.png: predator lost at t~580, prey then saturate

seeds_run.result: labkit pack to t=400: predator lost before t=400 (< 200 t)

verdicts.limitation: Supports the reading (a band of mixed outcomes at 240^2) and the pre-registered prediction (one of my two runle seeds also passes 500 t). With five runs at 240^2 the persistence times spread from < 200 to >= 700 t; this is not yet a probability per size, and the predation transfer is coded.
